statement: The depth ceiling takes effect before reading a map's key (TooDeep returns first even when the key is broken)
deviation: Nested `{"a": ...}` 64 times, and ended the 65th map header `a1` immediately with a **mid-cut text string header** `62 61` (declaring a length-2 text string but holding only 1 byte). The scanner reads a map's key via `item(depth + 1)`, so the 65th key reaches depth 65, becoming TooDeep at `depth > MAX_DEPTH` (64) before it has read even one byte of the key. Where D-65 passes through the array/map-value site, **this one alone discriminates the map's key-side `depth + 1`**: removing that addition would let the key pass at depth 64 and read the broken header, returning `Truncated`. ∴ the `expected_error` declaration is what catches the mutation. It violates no clause of 42 §2.1 (gx-policy, same as D-65).
